claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Conventional RAG retrieval for LLMs treats a large corpus of past issue tracking tickets as plain text, ignoring intra-issue structure and inter-issue relations, which limits performance.
claims.quote: The conventional retrieval methods in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for large language models (LLMs) treat a large corpus of past issue tracking tickets as plain text, ignoring the crucial intra-issue structure and inter-issue relations, which limits performance.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: The method constructs a knowledge graph from historical issues for retrieval, retaining intra-issue structure and inter-issue relations.
claims.quote: Our method constructs a KG from historical issues for use in retrieval, retaining the intra-issue structure and inter-issue relations.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: During question answering, the method parses consumer queries and retrieves related sub-graphs from the knowledge graph to generate answers.
claims.quote: During the question-answering phase, our method parses consumer queries and retrieves related sub-graphs from the KG to generate answers.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: Integrating a knowledge graph improves retrieval accuracy by preserving customer service structure information and enhances answering quality by mitigating text segmentation effects.
claims.quote: This integration of a KG not only improves retrieval accuracy by preserving customer service structure information but also enhances answering quality by mitigating the effects of text segmentation.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: On its benchmark datasets, the KG-RAG method outperformed the baseline by 77.6% in MRR and 0.32 in BLEU.
claims.quote: Empirical assessments on our benchmark datasets, utilizing key retrieval (MRR, Recall@K, NDCG@K) and text generation (BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR) metrics, reveal that our method outperforms the baseline by 77.6% in MRR and by 0.32 in BLEU.

claims.claim: The method was deployed within LinkedIn's customer service team for approximately six months and reduced median per-issue resolution time by 28.6%.
